title: [YouPass Collect] - Marriage age trends across decades
prompt: The charts below give information on the ages of people when they got married in one particular country in 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the percentages of males and females across six age groups who got married in a particular country in 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Overall
paragraphs: Overall, both genders demonstrated a clear trend towards marrying at older ages over the decade, with younger age brackets declining while older ones increased. Additionally, the 25-29 age group consistently had the highest marriage rates in both years, though by 2008, the 30-34 bracket for males nearly matched this figure.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the younger age groups, in 1998, nearly 12% of females got married between ages 25–29, roughly 3.5 percentage points higher than the corresponding male figure of around 8%. Meanwhile, 6% of women and just under 3% of men tied the knot in their early twenties (20–24), while teenage marriages (16–19) were virtually non-existent, at just 1% for females and a negligible 0% for males. By 2008, the 25–29 bracket remained relatively stable at nearly 12% for females and around 8% for males. The younger categories, however, witnessed dramatic declines, with the 20–24 group halving to approximately 3% for women and just over 1.5% for men, while teenage marriages became almost non-existent for both genders.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the older age brackets, in 1998, the 30-34 group recorded 7% for females and 9% for males, while the 35-39 and 40-44 categories showed progressively lower figures of 4% and 2% for women, compared to 7% and 5% for men. A decade later, the 30-34 bracket experienced substantial growth, rising to 8% for females and 11% for males, making it nearly as common as the 25-29 group. Similarly, the 35-39 age range increased modestly to 4.5% for women and 9% for men, while the oldest category (40-44) grew to 2.5% and 6.5% respectively.
